Well just a unfunny kidding.I use simple Chinese so that you or anyone can use translate machine to read it.:)

And therefore, I decided to put it through Google Translate to test the claim (I can read Chinese myself)… which gave me this:

To be honest, on the Chinese SCP, I do not like this is the most

Perhaps you feel that "not like" does not equate to "dissatisfaction", but yeah… it is not fully conducive if the average reader has to go through the trouble of translation algorithm. Besides, this "translation" alters your original opinion slightly.

中国的SCP

In the context of the article, I understand it refers to SCPs set in China. But Google translation (a common online translator) interprets that as "Chinese SCP", which could mean anything from "SCPs in Chinese language", "SCPs about China", or even "SCPs on the Chinese site".

And yes, context does help and one may claim I am nitpicking over the nuances of language. Regardless of intent, understanding a certain expression is important.

item.content:encoded:
At least one Foundation Agent who is fluent in Mandarin and is of obvious Chinese descent must be present; during an emergency, the former requirement is of higher priority.

If this is dated from the Qin Dynasty, why would Mandarin work at all? Mandarin (even Old Mandarin, the earliest form of the language) was only a thing during the Jurchen-led Jin Dynasty (making it concurrent with China's Song Dynasty; not to be confused with the Jin Dynasty ruled by the Sima clan after the Three Kingdoms era) or Yuan Dynasty.

If it were Qin Dynasty, they would have spoken Old Chinese instead.

item.content:encoded:
There are a couple of glaring problems with this one but apart from those it would be a definite upvote. I love the idea of terracotta soldiers on a steampunk spaceship :D Well thats the image I have in my head anyway, 'cept more Oriental in style and detailing ^^

Just some suggestions
– hide block

1. How do they communicate?
Sounds waves wont travel through a vacuum. They could possible touch the Foundation personal and send vibrations into their helmets? It would be cool for first contact if one researcher was excitedly chatting to one of them when the vibrations cause his faceplate to shatter. Could update the Containment Procedures with reference to the Incident :).

2. Why are they staying out of Imperial territory?
Surely they would be returning to their own territory? Why wouldnt they come back? This either needs a little explanation. I was thinking that maybe their ship was missing key components (like the missing sections in the archaeological evidence) and is unable to travel. When the Foundation offer to build one in exchange for the designs THEN the terracotta soldiers could refuse on grounds of national security :P

3. The nercromantic reference was extremely brief, could it be expanded upon?
'the notes on these sections indicate some kind of necromantic purpose intended for it'
Made me shudder a little, but I'd appreciate a little more to speculate on. Is the system linked to the ship or the crew? Is it a seperate entity itself? Is there any information about their surroundings (bomb doors, connection pipes or cables, etc)? If it isnt more specific you might as well say 'magical' in my opinion.

Really good article, still think it needs a little bit more though. ^^

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like the concept, but it's a little bare on details and/or scare factor. It's more weird than frightening. Is the supposed necromantic payload known to be some sort of superbomb containing zombie plague? Is the ship indestructible and therefore tends to destroy all opposition when disturbed, including passing spacecraft? And it seems a bit odd that they're in orbit all of this time, refusing to go past the moon towards Earth, when the only extant mission data was that they were to go to the sun to negotiate a treaty. Did they get lost? Run out of fuel? Successfully negotiate the treaty and retreat to the rendezvous point for a pickup that never happened?

As it is now, we have an object that is apparently of no threat, which the Foundation makes no effort to contain or to research. And that just doesn't feel like them. Observe is not part the SCP motto.
